title: Compiled Python bytecode artifact committed to the repository
evidence:
diff --git a/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f807a4d
Binary files /dev/null and b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc differ
--- and the .gitignore hunk adds only:
 *.dSYM/
+.pp-settings.bin
detail: A .pyc build artifact keyed to one interpreter (3.13) is now tracked. It silently goes stale the moment derive_a11y_palettes.py changes, and the .gitignore addition does not exclude __pycache__/, so regenerating it recreates the problem.
recommended_fix: git rm --cached the .pyc and add __pycache__/ (or tools/__pycache__/) to .gitignore.

title: Derivation script ships dead search machinery; its docstring claims a numeric search that does not exist
evidence:
def scale_lum(rgb, target_l):
    """Scale a color's luminance toward target_l, clamped (a crude but
    deterministic L shift — hue family is preserved to first order)."""
... def mix(a, b, t):  # linear mix in 8-bit space
... def verify(mode, remap, classes, tune=True):
    """Check every pair under the simulation on EFFECTIVE colors. Returns the
    (possibly empty) failure list — no silent auto-nudging: anchors are the
    canon; if a pair fails, HAND-TUNE the anchors above."""
    return [(lab, a, b, t) for lab, a, b, t in pair_list(mode, remap, classes)
            if dist(simulate(a, mode), simulate(b, mode)) < t]
--- while the module docstring promises: 4. Where a pair collides, search the mode-space remap: shift lightness (the axis that survives ALL three deficiencies) and nudge hue onto the deficiency's residual discriminable axis ... then numeric search.
detail: scale_lum and mix are never called anywhere in the script; verify's tune parameter is never read. The documented 'search' is fictional — all anchors are hand-set constants. The 'derivation record' misdescribes what it does.
recommended_fix: Delete scale_lum, mix, and the unused tune parameter, or implement the documented search; correct the module docstring to match the hand-anchor reality.

title: Script's 'paste verbatim' workflow cannot reproduce the shipped mode tables (packet_classes count mismatch)
detail: With nine catalog classes the script emits nine packet_classes entries; the shipped tables carry two. Usage says 'paste the "modes" block into data/palette.json verbatim' — following it produces data differing from what palcheck blessed.
recommended_fix: Emit only overridden classes (delta vs CLASS_BASE) so script output matches the shipped tables, or document that the committed block is a hand-trimmed subset.

title: Spec's frozen 'Always' bullet requires host/router tones to restyle per mode; no mode table remaps them
evidence:
spec-7-3: - Every mode restyles ALL of the view: state triad, lanes, ghost, roofs/host/router tones, packet class colors, water/coast/park map tokens, wire ribbons/crisis outline.
--- shipped deutan mode keys: state_healthy, state_congested, state_critical, lane_express, lane_standard, lane_best_effort, ghost_ok, ghost_bad, pipe_copper, pipe_steel, pipe_fiber, route_glow, route_tie, water, park, coast, house_roofs, packet_classes (no host_body / router entry in any of the three tables; base has "host_body": [62, 120, 208, 255])
--- script comment: # -- roofs/host/router accents: variety is decorative ... followed only by: remap["house_roofs"] = [(96, 38, 98), (178, 142, 74), (26, 98, 112), (58, 66, 94)]
detail: The frozen spec's Always constraint lists host/router tones among tokens every mode must restyle; the shipped tables and the derivation script remap house_roofs only. host_body keeps canon blue under every colorblind mode.
recommended_fix: Add host_body (and router tone) entries to each mode table and the script, or renegotiate the spec bullet to drop host/router.

title: Gate 2 command adds a setup step the adjacent comment explicitly forbids, under a stale label
evidence:
# gate 4's harness.sh mkdirs it — do NOT add setup steps to these commands.)
 GATES=(
   "Purity + grep gates (ODN-1)|tools/lint.sh"
-  "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|odin test core"
+  "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|mkdir -p bin && odin test core && odin test app -out:bin/app-test && odin test app/render -out:bin/render-test && odin test harness -out:bin/harness-test"
detail: The changed command prepends 'mkdir -p bin' directly after a comment saying 'do NOT add setup steps to these commands', and the label still reads 'Core unit tests' while the gate now builds and runs app, app/render, and harness test binaries.
recommended_fix: Move the mkdir to a pre-step (or rely on gate 4's) and rename the gate label to reflect the four test suites.

title: Spec Code Map names intents and an a11y verb syntax the implementation replaced
evidence:
spec: - `app/input/types.odin` + `poll/controller/touch` -- new Intents (Settings_Toggle, Panel_Navigate, Panel_Activate, Scale_Step); mapped on all devices
spec: - `harness/demo.odin` -- `a11y <mode>[,<mode>]` demo verb
--- _pr_body.md: new intents (`Toggle_Settings`, `Settings_Navigate`, `Settings_Activate`) mapped across keyboard (S, arrows, Enter, Esc), controller (Y, D-pad, A, B), and touch
--- demos use: a11y palette deutan / a11y reduced / a11y scale 150 (per-directive lines, no comma list)
detail: The frozen spec's Code Map lists four intents with different names (including a Scale_Step that no longer exists) and a comma-list verb syntax; the shipped implementation uses three renamed intents and per-directive demo lines. No change-log entry covers the drift.
recommended_fix: Add a spec Change Log entry (or amend the Code Map) recording the shipped intent names and the per-directive a11y syntax.

title: Palcheck separation threshold is routed by color-value equality on pr[0] only
detail: Pair classification (signal 48 vs map 40) is decided by comparing the first color's RGBA to map tokens. A future signal or packet-class token that coincidentally equals a map color silently gets the weaker threshold; pr[1] is never considered.
recommended_fix: Tag each pair with an explicit kind (signal/map) at append time instead of post-hoc color-equality routing.
